By evening it's built a nest out of your essay, and you don't mind.|You keep it warm in your pocket all day. Nobody notices; it glows when you laugh.|You carry it about in your hood all day. It hoots once in the middle of a lecture, and you cough to cover it, heroically.} Take it to the stables {~You walk it down to the stables. Professor Brask tells it, very kindly, where hedge-sprites belong, and tells you, less kindly, to check your bag.|Professor Brask takes the newt in her palm and tells you three things about cave newts you'll never forget. You miss it a bit on the walk back.|Professor Brask tucks the owlet into a nest box and tells you where its mother is likely to be. You find yourself checking your hood all week.}
